newsitem.title: USA: U.S. CASH SOYMEAL - SOME BASIS OFFERS FALL SHARPLY.
newsitem.headline: U.S. CASH SOYMEAL - SOME BASIS OFFERS FALL SHARPLY.

text.p: Soymeal basis offers in some U.S. truck and rail markets fell sharply on Friday, under pressure from dealers' eagerness to sell, merchandisers said.
"The bean movement has kind of shut off and now people just want to move the product," said one Indiana crusher.
Dealers also said that crushers were eager to sell as much soymeal as they could basis CBOT August futures because August holds a stiff premium to July.
"Sellers are getting nervous because they don't want to sell it against the Sepember," said one soybean crusher from the southeast.
At 1030 CDT, the August/September soybean spreading was trading near 25.00 per ton.

The National Oilseed Processors Association reported a weekly crush of 23.549 million bushels. That figure was within trade expectations for 22.00 million to 24.20 million and slightly below last week's crush of 23.58 million.
